paper.abstract_en: The discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos has recently prompted interest in the role of gravity in neutrino flavor conversion. In this work, we investigate the gravity-modulated CP violation (CPV) in neutrino oscillations in the Reissner--Nordström and Hayward spacetimes. Employing analytical and numerical methods, we reveal the interplay among the CPV, the properties of neutrinos, and the space-time. The shapes of the flavor-oscillation curves show that CPV signals encode both space-time geometry and mass ordering, and that the imprints of $m_l$ are intrinsically correlated with the singular versus nonsingular structure of the background metric. In particular, our finding demonstrate that the CPV observables exceed the limitation that, in asymptotically flat space-time, gravity neither damps nor amplifies neutrino-oscillation amplitudes.
